claim: GigE Vision 3.0 was approved by the GigE Vision Technical Committee on 17 April 2026 at IVSM Prague and its release was announced by A3 on 12-13 May 2026; it adds RDMA over RoCEv2 via a new GigE Vision RDMA Streaming Protocol (GVRSP) and expands the control channel to carry more data per packet.
how_verified: read-spec/doc (curl + text extraction of A3 pages)

claim: GigE Vision 3.0 is a supplement to GVSP: 3.0 cameras support GVSP v2 plus GVRSP, legacy GVSP v1 is not supported in 3.0, RDMA/GVRSP is optional (not all 3.0 cameras support it), and using it requires a RoCEv2-capable NIC plus a GVRSP-capable library.

None of the A3 GigE Vision 3.0 materials read (press release, FAQ, standard page, Industry Insight, RoCEv2 pre-announcement) mention PTP, IEEE 1588, timestamps or synchronization; GVCP is retained for discovery/configuration.

claim: IEEE 1588 PTP, unconditional and scheduled action commands, ActionLate, link aggregation, PAUSE frames, 10GigE and compressed payloads (JPEG, JPEG 2000, H.264) were introduced in GigE Vision 2.0 (November 2011).

GigE Vision 2.1 (Aug 2018) added multi-part payload and an updated IEEE1588 profile, exposed via IEEE1588 Extended Capability (0x0974), Supported Profiles (0x0978; 'PTP profile' bit 0x80000000, '802.1AS profile' bit 0x40000000) and Selected Profile (0x097C) registers; IEEE's PTP profile registry lists 'GigE Vision 2.1' (AIA) as a profile document.
GigE Vision 2.2 (June 2022) added GenDC streaming (payload type 0x000B) and multi-event data; MultiZone payload was deprecated in 2.2.

GigE Vision 1.0 was released May 2006; 1.1 announced 23 Apr 2009 (pixel/Bayer formats, error handling, GenICam schema versions, action commands to multiple devices); 1.2 announced 21 Jan 2010 (non-streaming device control).

The GenICam/SFNC PTP feature set (PtpEnable, PtpStatus, PtpOffsetFromMaster, etc.) references IEEE 1588-2008; the Ptp* features were added in SFNC 2.4 (June 2018) replacing deprecated GevIEEE1588*; SFNC 2.8 (2026-04-08) contains no RDMA/GVRSP features.
how_verified: read-spec/doc (pdftotext of SFNC 2.8, sections 27.3, 27.4.38-40, history table)

claim: Basler states its cameras support IEEE 1588-2008 (PTPv2), map PTP time to the 64-bit GigE Vision timestamp, and default to end-to-end delay measurement (ace 2/dart M can select a peer-to-peer default profile).

The 'single cable' capability comes from combining PoE (IEEE 802.3af/at, separate standards) with GigE Vision 2.x PTP + (scheduled) action commands, letting the Ethernet cable carry data, power and trigger.

A host can read the implemented spec version from bootstrap register 0x0000 (major<<16 | minor), also present at the start of DISCOVERY_ACK, and PTP/scheduled-action support from GVCP Capability 0x0934 (IEEE1588 0x00080000, Scheduled Action 0x00020000, Unconditional Action 0x00100000, 1588 ext caps 0x00010000, Action 0x00000040); ACTION_CMD is 0x0100 with an optional 64-bit scheduled time when flag 0x80 is set.
how_verified: read-code + ran-test (docker ubuntu:24.04, arv-fake-gv-camera-0.8 + python3 -I probe.py 127.0.0.1; decoded synthetic 0x00020001/0x001B0067 as v2.1 + IEEE1588 + ScheduledAction)

claim: Aravis (main @482547a3, 2026-10-22) has no host-side ACTION_CMD or PTP register support (GVCP command enum ends at PENDING_ACK 0x0089; only Action bit defined among action/PTP capability bits), and neither Aravis nor Wireshark contains any RDMA/RoCE/GVRSP code.
Aravis's fake GigE Vision camera leaves the Version (0x0000) and GVCP Capability (0x0934) registers at 0, so it cannot emulate PTP or scheduled action capabilities.
